36 line 1: the other witness reads அருளுடையெம் for அருளுடையேம்.
39 line 3: சூதின் கண்தாங்கால் looks like a misprint for சூதின்கண் தாங்கல், the verbal noun the other items have.
40 line 1: விறலு மகளிர்கட்கு splits விறலும் across the word break.
33 line 4: படைவேந்தன் மற்று விடல் is obscure and may be corrupt.

reading: Living by giving away a quarter of what comes in, the distinction of not raking over what was done when strife arose, and learning the good things after weighing many are named the excellence that good men hold to.
nuance: The giving is fixed as a share, கால் (a quarter) of income, not left to feeling. செருவாய்ப்பச் செய்தவை most likely means what others did to one when a quarrel arose, so the second item is forgiveness; the verse does not say whose deeds they were.

reading: The fetter called attachment, the chariot of craving that runs down many roads with its clinging never cut, and the hostile darkness called false speech are named three things with whose seed destroyed birth itself perishes.
nuance: Each fault is given an image (a rope, a runaway chariot, a darkness), and the third is a fault of speech set among two inner cravings as a cause of rebirth. The other witness reads புகையிருள் (smoky darkness) for பகையிருள், which changes the image but not the claim.

reading: The worth of giving gifts, the conduct of men of honour that has driven out faults, and a mind that has left many possessions behind are named a rope that binds good deeds for anyone.
nuance: கயிறு, a rope, makes the three things the means by which merit is held or drawn up; the third item is a renouncer's detachment, set beside a householder's giving as the same kind of rope.

reading: The sweet words from the mouth of a courtesan with lovely soft shoulders, the frog hidden as bait inside a fishhook, and the bowing of hardened enemies are named a mire that sinks those who step in.
nuance: All three are pleasing surfaces over a harm: speech, bait and homage. The predicate அளறு (mire) adds that the harm is not a blow but a slow sinking.

reading: The verse reports that those who have learnt and understood do not eat from the hand of three: the petty man who lives by arrogance, the bangled woman who sells her body for a price, and the man who destroyed an endowment set apart for the good.
nuance: The grounds given are moral, not ritual: all three live by a wrong (pride, sale of the body, theft of a charity). அறப்புறம் is property dedicated to charity, so the third man has robbed the good themselves.

norm.note: a commensality rule of the period: whose food the learned refuse, a courtesan among them

reading: The guest who knows what his host can afford, the man who lives having put away the killing of precious life, and the teacher richly possessed of sweet good conduct are named the ones who are called the world.
nuance: The guest is judged here, not the host: the courtesy asked of him is to know the measure of the house. ஞாலம் எனப்படுவார் means that such people are what 'the world' properly means, as உலகம் often means the worthy.

reading: Bathing before eating at mealtime, not speaking with partiality whatever one may gain, and not letting one's nobility fail even if the skin dries and one dies are named the work of those who call themselves pure.
nuance: The list joins a rule of bodily purity to two inner ones without ranking them; the predicate (தூஉயம் என்பார், those who say 'we are pure') makes all three the test of a claim to purity.

norm.note: a purity rule of the period: bathing before the meal

reading: The man without austerity who speaks in anger wanting to win, the man who sits craving what he does not have, and the man who listens to learning only to watch for faults are named three who pound husk and tire their hands.
nuance: The image of pounding husk (உமி) is labour with no grain in it: each of the three spends effort where nothing can come of it. நோன்பிலி names anger to win as a lack of austerity.

reading: Not falling from one's own course even when a woman desires one and follows, having no longing for a thing even when the eye craves it and it comes to hand, and not prizing a span of life that ends in falling to the earth are named the view of the learned who sought out subtle things.
nuance: Each item is a restraint under the strongest temptation (the woman follows, the thing is already in hand). மண்விழுந்து வாழ்நாள் மதியாமை is hard: it may mean not counting on a life that falls to earth, or not reckoning days spent sunk in the world; the reading takes the first.

reading: One who does not scorn those who come to him in need, one who has put away heedlessness in settled wealth, and one who has always kept clear of envy are named three whose fame endures.
nuance: The second item puts the danger of heedlessness in wealth that seems secure (மன்னிய செல்வம்), the moment one stops guarding it.

reading: Learning the good among many things, carrying on without break the household life of sharing one's food, and making wealth firmly by one's own effort are named the head of all that is taught.
nuance: The three are learning, giving and earning, and the third supplies the second: the household shares what its own labour (தாள்) made.

reading: Grasping the meaning by attending to subtle words, not speaking empty words unfit for learning even when asked, and speaking good words only to those who are not base are named the debt the learned have taken on.
nuance: One duty of hearing and two of speaking; கடன் (debt) makes them obligations that come with learning, not graces.

reading: Subjects who live in awe of the sceptre, a minister who holds the people close like the aerial roots of a banyan, and the protection of a man firm as the bead at a spear's butt are named three that a king with an army does not let go.
nuance: The closing words படைவேந்தன் மற்று விடல் are obscure: they may mean the king must not let these go, or that a king without them is to be left; the reading takes the first. The banyan's aerial roots both hold the tree up and spread it.
domain_note: the king, his minister and his guard

reading: The brahmin who has discharged the three debts, the king who weighs matters and does not bend justice, and the people who keep within bounds without turbulence are named the ones who are called the world.
nuance: பார்ப்பான் is a birth-group term here, defined by a ritual duty; the verse does not name the three debts, which tradition identifies as owed to sages, gods and ancestors. The verse sets priest, king and people side by side as the order that makes a 'world'.
domain_note: the three estates of a kingdom

norm.note: a varna norm of the period: the brahmin is defined by his three ritual debts

reading: A mind of genius that does not rise and toss like the waves of the sea, one who with great hearing of subtle texts has seen the far shore of learning, and one who without darkness of nature cuts away delusion are named three who stand on true nature.
nuance: மயலுறுப்பான் is read as மயல் அறுப்பான் (who cuts away delusion); taken as மயல் உறுப்பான் it would say the opposite. The first item may also mean a genius that rises above the sea's waves.

reading: One who eats flesh and says he has compassion for living beings, one who says the killing is done without his own consent, and one who kills in a sacrifice he desires are named three who know only what they themselves have seen fit to see.
nuance: All three are self-justifications for taking life: a claim of compassion, a denial of complicity (the buyer who says someone else killed), and the merit of sacrifice. The closing line is ironic: their knowledge is only their own way of seeing.

norm.note: the period's dispute over flesh-eating and animal sacrifice, stated as the verse's judgment against both

reading: The measure of friendship shows in backbiting, lineage shows in a fullness of character pleasant to meet, and authority shows in a purity like milk; these three are named the way of those who hold to truth.
nuance: Each item is a sign by which something hidden is known. பிரமாணம் (measure, authority) and the predicate வாய்மை யடையார் வழக்கு are uncertain; அடையார் could also be negative ('those who have not attained truth'), which would reverse the predicate.

reading: Admiring oneself and swelling with pride, swelling anger in vain without humility, and the meanness of coveting the many things one has set one's mind on are named an army that breaks wealth.

Seeking the base stupor of embracing women bought with wealth, living drunk on toddy from the cup, and, scorning honest speech, bearing the stupor of lies at the dice are named the work of men without goodness.
nuance: Each item carries மயக்கம் (stupor), so sex for pay, drink and dice are made three kinds of intoxication. புலை here means the vile or fleshly, not a person; it is not used as a caste term.

reading: The strength that wears anger thin, having conduct befitting toward women, and attaining the good wisdom of eating after sharing are named the work of those of ancient wisdom.
nuance: மகளிர்கட்கு ஒத்த லொழுக்கம் is read as a man's fitting conduct toward women (his wife); it could also be read as conduct that suits women, a rule for them. Anger is measured by quantity (நுணுக்கும், thinning), the counterpart of verse 38's swelling.

norm.note: a marital norm of the period on conduct toward women; the phrase allows more than one reading

title: திரிகடுகம் 41-60
theme: Verses 41 to 60 count, three at a time, what heads instruction, what makes a family fair or brings it down, what leads to hell or stops the rain, what the wise avoid and what is wasted, and close on the sorrow proper to every kind of birth; household, royal and inward conduct are judged on one scale.
source_issues: 41 lines 2-3: அன்போடி stands before the dash and seems to run into line 3; it is taken as அன்போடு, 'with affection'.
45 line 3: the count word is fused with the verb (தானுமிம் மூவர்), so count_word records மூவர் and the third item stops at சிந்தியா.
46: printed without a number and numbered 46 by its place after 45; line 4 repeats the closing line of verse 14.
50 line 2 lacks the dash that marks the caesura in the other verses.
51 line 1: தூர்ந்துஒழுகிக் is obscure and may be corrupt; the count word is written as one word, இவர்மூவர்.
57 lines 1-3: தட்டித்துப் and துச்சிருந்தான் ஆளும் கலங்கா முறுதலும் are hard to divide; the word boundary in கலங்கா முறுதலும் (கலம் காமுறுதல்) is taken as printed.

reading: Renown from giving something to those in distress, the worth that keeps one's family standing from sinking even when shaken, and adding to one's friends day by day with affection are named the three chief of all that is heard.
nuance: The predicate கேள்வியுள் எல்லாந் தலை ranks three practices above everything learnt by hearing, so the verse measures instruction by what it should make a person do; the second item concedes that the family may be shaken (துளங்கினும்) and asks only that its worth not fall.

reading: Not coveting wealth that comes from the gaming hall, behaving toward brahmins as toward fire even when familiar with them, and living with a love of farming are said to be the beauty of the vellala family.
nuance: பார்ப்பார் is a birth-group term and the rule ranks it: the cultivating family is to keep the distance and caution one keeps with fire however close the acquaintance. The verse defines a family's beauty by occupation and by its bearing toward another birth-group, beside a refusal of gambling gain.

norm.note: a birth-rank rule of the period: the conduct a cultivating family is to keep toward brahmins

reading: Restraint of the mouth is purity, restraint of deed without stain is the divine state, and restraint of the heart without falsehood is release; these three are things free of deceit.
nuance: The three restraints rise in order, mouth, deed, heart, and their fruits rise with them, from purity to the heavenly (திப்பியம்) to release (வீடு), so the verse is a ladder rather than a list of equals. மாசற்ற may also be read with துப்புரவாம் (stainless purity) rather than with செய்கை.

reading: A day on which one ate without a guest, a night on which one did not turn to embrace one's well-adorned wife, and a morning on which one went off without giving to the needy are a sickness to the strong-minded.
nuance: The three items run through the whole day, day, night and morning (பகல், கங்குல், காலை), so the householder's day is judged complete only when guest, wife and the poor have each had their share; the sickness falls on உரனுடையார், the strong, as if neglect were felt only by those fit to do these duties.

reading: The one who torments a man who cannot do a thing by telling him to do it, the one who without love hides from those who ask what he could give, and the one who does not think on the certainty of Death's coming are three who fall into hell.
nuance: The third man has done nothing to anyone: forgetting death is set beside cruelty and concealment as an offence of equal weight, so heedlessness itself earns hell.

reading: A spirited horse whose feet are not sound, a fierce elephant with no clean seat above, and the place of one who snarls, nurses rancour and speaks in rage are three things the wise do not go near.
nuance: கால்தூய்மை and மேல்தூய்மை are obscure: they may mean a horse not sure of foot and an elephant with no trained rider on its back, or untamed beasts generally. பள்ளி may be the angry man's dwelling or his company. The verse sets an angry man among dangerous animals.

reading: Women of few words and broad shoulders, the choice wealth one has brought in by many kinds of effort, and food prepared so that it makes the tongue flourish are three things whose guarding must not be slighted.
nuance: Women are counted among the goods of the house with earned treasure and good food, all three needing watch; the verse reports the custodial view of women of its period. காப்பிகழ் ஆகா may also be read as 'not to be scorned', which would make the line a praise of the three rather than a rule of keeping them.

norm.note: a household norm of the period that counts women among the goods a man must guard

reading: The one who takes abuse as sweet speech, the one who values gruel as rice poured with ghee, and the one who eats seeping bitterness accepting it as sugar are three who live having seen the true thing.
nuance: Each item takes a bad thing as its opposite, in speech, in food and in taste, and the verse calls this not endurance but sight of the true (மெய்ப்பொருள் கண்டு): the bitter is not borne as bitter, it is no longer judged so.

reading: Young kin who set aside what they are bidden, a head of the house who keeps no guard and speaks in abuse and scorn, and a wife who wears that house down through falsehood are three who are no security for this life.
nuance: ஏவாது மாற்றும் may mean 'refuses without being asked' or 'sets aside the bidding'; பொய்தெள்ளி ('sifting falsehood') is unclear. The verse spreads the failure of a house over its junior, its head and its wife, each by a fault of speech or obedience.

norm.note: a judgment of the period on a wife's conduct in the house, set beside those on kin and husband

reading: A king who covets goods to seize and harasses his people, men of deceitful speech who do not say what is within, and a woman who, living in the house, crosses its bounds are three ill planets that swiftly cut off the rain.
nuance: கோள் is a malign planet: the verse gives three human faults the astrological power to stop rain, ranging from the throne through common men to a wife, so the cosmic sanction the Kural gives to the king is spread over the whole society.

norm.note: a rule of the period binding a wife's conduct to the household's bounds, and her transgression to drought

reading: Allies remain allies even when they keep their distance, deceivers remain deceivers even when they keep close, and the base are hurtful like a split stone; these three, when examined, show what they are.
nuance: தூர்ந்துஒழுகி is obscure: read with தூரா in verse 56 it means 'when the way is closed', so the ally stays an ally even when estranged. ஈர்ந்தகல் may be a sawn stone that cannot rejoin, an image for the base. The point is constancy of nature under changed conduct.

reading: Kindly regard is the ornament of the eye, modesty the ornament of a woman in love, and learning the ornament for the life to come; these three are found only in those who bear the mark of worth.
nuance: Each item has its own wearer (the eye, a woman, the next life), and the closing line gathers them: the three are not acquired apart but are found together in the குறியுடையார். The modesty item assigns naanam to women specifically.

norm.note: a gender norm of the period: modesty assigned as the woman's ornament

reading: The beauty of a blind man's wife, the eager talk of a man without learning that clears darkness, and listening to the lute by one who cannot tell its modes are three things that come to nothing when weighed.
nuance: Two items are waste on the receiver's side (beauty unseen, music unheard), and the middle one, the unlearned man's eager speech, is put among them: his talk is like a gift with no one able to take it, or a skill with nothing behind it.

reading: Attaching oneself to those who do not weigh one's good, speaking of benefits one will not yield oneself in a moment of anger, and charging others with faults when the charge bears no later fruit are the doings of those without clear sense.
nuance: The lines are compressed and each item admits more than one parse (தன்பயம் may be one's own good or the other's; காய்வின்கண் may be 'in anger' or 'toward the angry'). The common thread is action without regard to its result, which the closing word தெற்றெனவு (clarity) names.

reading: A friendship that does not keep a weighty secret, a woman who has abandoned the wish for honour, and a petty servant who nurses rancour wherever he is are three who are called spies.
nuance: ஒற்றாள் here is not the king's agent but the leak inside one's own circle: friend, woman and servant become informers against the one they are close to. The woman item reports a judgment of the period on women's honour.

norm.note: a judgment of the period that counts a woman without regard for honour among informers

reading: First learning the letters as they come, then serving father and mother, and joining the great road of conduct handed down are the three ways by which the path of excellence is not blocked.
nuance: முந்தை and பிற்பாடு make this a sequence of life, not a list: letters first, then the parents, then inherited conduct; and the predicate is negative, these keep the road of விழுப்பம் from being choked (தூரா).

reading: Song not measured to the beat, the clamour of one who enters to beg and eat, and a lodger's craving for the vessels his host uses are three things painful to hear.
nuance: தட்டித்து and துச்சிருந்தான் ஆளும் கலம் are hard: the second item may be a beggar knocking and shouting, the third a guest in borrowed quarters who covets the master's vessels. The frame கேள்வியுள் echoes verse 41, which names what is best to hear.

reading: Giving with regard to old ties, embracing kin by right so that they rejoice, and gathering one's people with close words are the work of the king's younger.
nuance: The kin-work is assigned not to the king but to the one younger than him: holding the royal kin together is a delegated office. இளையான் may be the younger brother or any junior in the royal line.
domain_note: the king's younger brother or junior prince

reading: The wealth of one who does not help his kin, the farming of one who does not tend the green crop at ripening, and the family standing of one who lives drinking toddy while young perish while seeming to exist.
nuance: உள்ளன போலக் கெடும் says the ruin is hidden: each thing still appears to be there while it is already lost, so the verse warns against judging by possession.

reading: Great hunger in the birth of a ghost, fear in the birth of a beast, and the misery of want in the birth of humans who cannot discern are three that make birth a birth of sorrow.
nuance: Each kind of birth is given its own sorrow, so no birth escapes: the human's is not hunger or fear but want (நிரப்பிடும்பை), and புலம்தெரியா makes it the lot of humans who cannot see clearly.

title: திரிகடுகம் 61-80
theme: Twenty verses of three things each range from the minister's daily practice to the wife's debts, the passions that consume their holder, what counts as wealth and purity, and gifts wasted on those who lack their inner condition; again and again a good is measured by the giving, restraint or trust within the person rather than by outward rank.
source_issues: thirikadugam 76 line 1: the text reads வருந்தும் where the sense and tamilvu have விருந்தும் (guest); the item is copied as written.

reading: Conducting oneself so that the fivefold knowledge comes within reach, guarding in advance so that what threatens to arrive does not arrive, and knowing day by day the state of the kings who stand opposed are named the settled practice of great ministers of renown.
nuance: ஐயறிவும் is the hard word: it may be the knowledge of the five senses held in order, or fivefold learning a minister must have; either way the first item is a discipline of the self and the other two face outward, to the coming danger and the hostile king. The count word is the personal இம்மூவர் though the three things are practices, not persons.

reading: The shameless man who does not weigh the worth of a kindness done him, the man who speaks crookedly in the public assembly before the worthy, and the man who wrongly keeps a deposit placed with him are named three who live on with their line of descendants lost.
nuance: எச்சம் இழந்து names the punishment in the next generation, not in the offender's own life: all three faults are breaches of trust (a kindness, a public judgment, a deposit), and the verse makes the loss of heirs their common wage.

reading: Friendship with those who do not shrink from causing pain, keeping in the house a bangled wife who dreads guests, and living beside people whose nature yields no worth are named three things that bring no good.
nuance: All three are about who lives near one: a friend, a wife, a neighbour. The wife's fault is not unchastity but fear of guests, so the house fails at the outward duty the next verse assigns her.

reading: By tending good guests she is a friend, by daily caring for the household she is the mother who bore it, and by bearing children of an old family she is the mistress of the house: these three are named the debts a chaste wife has taken on.
nuance: Each duty earns a role (friend, mother, mistress), so the wife is three persons to the house; the closing word கடன் makes them owed, and கற்புடையாள் makes chastity the frame within which all three are counted.

norm.note: a rule of the period for a wife's duties: hospitality, care of the house and bearing children are her debts as a chaste woman

reading: Fear rising like the wave-tossed sea, craving that cannot let go of what it has longed for, and anger that cannot see the true state of what is bound up with it are said to be the way one fries in one's own ghee.
nuance: The image is self-consumption: the fat that cooks one is one's own, so the three passions need no outside enemy. Fear stands where a quick reader expects confusion beside desire and anger.

reading: The adornment of a woman who has no husband, the ring on the hand of a man who has no servant to walk behind him, and a king who lives having bent the sceptre he holds are named three things not joined with fitness.
nuance: கறை is uncertain: read as dark adornment, the first two items are both ornaments worn without the support that makes them fitting (a husband, a servant), and the king's bent sceptre becomes the same kind of empty sign; read as 'stain', the first item would be a widow's blame, and the parallel weakens.

norm.note: a rule of the period on a woman without a husband: her adornment is counted unfitting

reading: A wife who stands against her husband, servants without proper nature, and kin who stand in fault are said to devour a man, as his hair greys, like the fruit of his old deeds, and there is nothing the sufferer can do about them.
nuance: முந்தை பழவினையாய் makes the three household troubles the shape that past karma takes, which is why the verse ends that the sufferer has no remedy: they are borne, not fixed.

reading: Having wealth that gives something to those who have nothing, the right way of one who considers the impermanence of this world, and the purity that does nothing painful to any creature are named three things found in people who know the good.
nuance: தூய்மை is defined here by an act toward others, not by bathing or diet: purity is harming no living thing.

reading: An ox that does hard work, a maiden of well-formed full body long kept at home, and a guest who arrives in distress having strayed from the road are named three things hard to come by.
nuance: The guest is counted as a prize, beside a draught ox and a marriageable girl, not as a burden; the lost and suffering guest is the most valued because he most needs the house.

norm.note: a period valuation of a young woman's body and seclusion, counted among prized possessions with the ox

reading: One who dug a tank for charity with a grove beside it, the brahmin who has reached the far shore of the Veda by recitation, and one who, avoiding evil, eats after sharing what he can are the three called rich.
nuance: Wealth is redefined as what one has given or mastered: a public work, learning held on the tongue, and food shared. பார்ப்பான் names a birth group, but the verse praises his learning and states no rule of rank.

reading: The bathing of those who have no cloth to change into, women who take up and enter the disputation of the assembly, and the poverty of men who have the manliness to give and protect are named three things the poet's eye cannot bear to see.
nuance: The first person என் கண் is rare in the book. The line division is doubtful: பெண்டிர் may close the first item (women bathing without a change of cloth) rather than open the second; on the reading taken here, women in the assembly's contest are counted as an unbearable sight. காண அரிய could also mean simply 'rarely seen'.

norm.note: a period judgment that women entering the assembly's disputation is an unfitting sight

reading: Poverty fears the man of steady heart, ill-gotten wealth fears the man who keeps dharma in mind, and every creature fears the warrior: these three are named matters settled by strength.
nuance: The grammar is reversed from the expected: the man does not avoid poverty or wrong wealth, they avoid him, so his inner strength acts on things outside him the way the warrior's acts on creatures.

reading: The man who says he will make bright wealth by begging, the man who calls a woman who goes about with many his bond of love, and the man who sails across the wide sea are named three who live daring what is hard.
nuance: The sea voyage is a real risk set beside two risks of judgment, so begging for wealth and trusting a wanton woman are made as perilous as open water.

norm.note: a period judgment on a woman's conduct: a woman who goes about widely is no fit bond

reading: The man who lives by killing and eating, the fool who presumes to embrace the great when they embrace, and the man who laughs at one who says 'I have nothing, give me something' are named three who hold fast to nothing.
nuance: கடைப்பிடியாதார் is the common fault: none keeps a rule. The second item is unsure: it may be the fool who takes the familiarity of the great as licence to be familiar himself, or one who clings only when the great cling to him.

reading: Wealth in the hands of one bound to generosity, the books learned by one with understanding in his heart, and a leader who knows what is fitting in his alliances are named three trees whose wood has hardened without a hollow.
nuance: காழ்த்த மரம் is heartwood, prized for being solid through: the image values soundness within, not fruit given out. புணர்வு may be alliance, counsel or marriage, and the leader is left open.

reading: A guest who comes on a rainy day, a courtesan whose heart is elsewhere yet who never falls short in her business, and a servant who in his valour answers back against a command are named three who are hard to tend even when one tries.
nuance: Our text reads வருந்தும், which would make the first item 'the one who suffers on a rainy day'; the count and the sense want விருந்தும், the guest. The three are hard to keep for different reasons: the guest's need, the courtesan's divided heart, the servant's pride.

norm.note: a period view of the courtesan as a woman whose divided heart makes her hard to keep

reading: Living out of reach of the base, keeping friendship with the good without forsaking them even in the dead of night, and carefully guarding that nothing scarring comes are named three things found only in those whose family is spotless.
nuance: The closing ஏ (உள்ளார்க்கே) restricts the three to the spotless family: the verse reads conduct as the sign of lineage rather than lineage as a licence.

reading: Having purity is boldness, having truthfulness that drives off evil deeds is beauty, and not uttering evil in mind or speech: these three are named the practice of those who have grown strong in penance.
nuance: The first two items carry their own predicates (purity is boldness, truth is beauty) inside the count; துணிவாம் தொழிலகற்றும் could also be read together as 'truth that removes rash deeds', which would shift the first item's predicate.

reading: The man who lives without fearing blame, who is a cow; the man who through decline gave up the hard penance he took on; and the man who, having married, lives in fear of his wife, who is an ox: that these three eat rice is a sickness to the heart.
nuance: இவர்மூவர் is a personal form, so the cow and the ox are men called beasts; the predicate is that their being fed at all grieves the onlooker. The first item could instead be the cow of a blameless-fearless man, which the count word argues against.

norm.note: a period judgment on a husband who lives in fear of his wife

reading: Leadership gained by one who does not rule justly, penance taken up by one without restraint of heart, and beauty gained by one who does not make his conduct perfect are named seed scattered into a thicket.
nuance: Each item is a gain (rank, penance, beauty) that comes to someone who lacks its inner condition, so the waste lies in the receiver, not in the gift.

title: திரிகடுகம் 81-100
theme: Verses 81 to 100 count threes under predicates of loss and power: those who sink in craving, who are born yet unborn, who are utter fools or miss the good world, set against the wife, ascetic, king and priest whose keeping of their station brings rain, with the spy and the king's limbs closing the book on rule.
source_issues: 95: the verse is printed without a number and is numbered 95 by its place after 94.
95 line 2: the source prints செறிவழங்கத்; tamilvu has செறிவு அழுங்கத், which the reading follows.
96 line 1: குறிப்பறிவான் is a masculine form attached to பெண்டாட்டி; a feminine form would be expected.
96 line 3: the misprint சொய்வான் was repaired to செய்வான், as tamilvu; the reading differs from the site.
100 line 4: மேந்தர்க்கு is most likely a misprint for வேந்தர்க்கு.
89 line 3: இறந்து இன்னா is printed with a space and no sandhi, unlike the rest of the text.
88 line 3: இயங்கலிவை fuses the end of the third item with the count word இவை; the item and count word are given as the text runs.

reading: The courtesan who lives by offering her shoulders like a public ford, the gambler without decency who looks to the gaming hall every day, and the man who makes bright wealth by taking a premium on money are named three who sink in the sea of craving.
nuance: The three are not the customers of vice but those who live by it: the seller of the body, the professional gambler and the money-dealer. வாசி is read here as the premium or discount taken in exchanging or lending money; the word allows other trades, so the third figure is the least certain.

reading: Being called worthy among the worthy at all times, being called close among those who are close, and not saying, even when roused to spring up, what those who will not take it would not accept are named three as the way a good person offers.
nuance: The first two are standings given by peers, the third a restraint one keeps oneself, so the verse makes reputation and silence one path. நல்லாள் can be a good person or a good woman; nothing else in the verse points to a woman, so it is read generally.

reading: A great heap of salt is gone if water soaks it, the rich shoot of friendship is gone if a lie is dealt, and the upright are like rain; these three are named a way the path of rectitude is kept from being choked.
nuance: Two items are images of dissolution and the third an image of giving, and the closing predicate (செப்பநெறி தூரா ஆறு) has to cover both; it is read as lessons that keep the straight path open, which is a guess at how the list holds together.

reading: A tank whose inlet is not well made, an infant that has not drunk its fill at its mother's breast, and people of a long line who lack the excellence of learning are named three joined to poverty.
nuance: All three fail to take in what should fill them: water, milk, learning. சேய்மரபில் is read as 'in a long or distant line'; it could instead mean those of a far-off or lesser descent, which would change who the third item faults.

reading: Being of a kind that people scorn, a sharpness that does not forget a secret once heard, and the perception that reports the hidden matter without fail are named the three qualities of a spy worth considering.
nuance: The first quality is not a virtue but a cover: to belong to a despised kind is to be overlooked, and the verse counts it among qualities on the same footing as memory and judgment.

reading: The loosening and ending of the great tie of love, letting go of the great raft of chastity out of desire, and the loss of friendship's gracious nature are named three as an enmity that brings fault.
nuance: The three are bonds (a tie, a raft, a nature) and their breaking is called an enmity, as if the broken bond turns into an enemy. Whose chastity is let go is not said: it can be a wife's lapse or, as verse 97 suggests, a husband's casting off a chaste wife for another desire.

reading: One who, without fear, wants to kill, one who goes into a company far from learning, and one who sits idle and lets great wealth dwindle are named three fit to be utter fools.

The way one suffers when disease eats at him, the way great Death, never abating, consumes life, and wealth tied to one moving on without worth are named three ways that unsettle the standing of the raft.
nuance: The raft (புணை) is most likely the body or the life it carries. The third item is the hardest: பிணைசெல்வம் may be wealth bound to one, or pledged wealth, and மாண்பின்று இயங்கல் may mean it passes away without dignity; the reading given is one of several the words allow. The count word is fused by sandhi with the third item (இயங்கலிவை மூன்றும்), so only மூன்றும் is given as written.

reading: One who gives grace no room in his heart, one who buries wealth without enjoying it, and one who oversteps and speaks hurtful words are named three who, though born, are as if never born.

The verse names earning wealth for the sake of giving, learning the great books so as to join the path of dharma, and speaking words always with grace as three ways not to reach the world of darkness.
nuance: This is one of the few verses in the book in the imperative (செய்க, சொல்லுக); each item gives a purpose to a means, wealth for giving and books for dharma, so earning and study are judged by their end.

reading: Speaking heedlessly at the moment of gain, saying at the end 'we have lost our life', and feeling shame when a blemish comes and one's own body withers are named three signs of the body that does not last.
nuance: The predicate can mean signs that the body is passing (marks of approaching death) or the marks of one who lives as if the body were not passing; the first item, heedless speech at a gain, fits the second sense better, the second and third the first.

reading: One not born in an excellent family line, the wretch who understands not a single letter, and one who always delights in excessive speech are named three who, though born, are as if never born.
nuance: விழுத்திணை is read as a high birth-group or lineage (திணை as kind or clan), which makes the first item a rule about birth ranked with two faults of learning and speech. If திணை is read as conduct, the item would fault character instead; the birth reading is the plainer one.

norm.note: a birth-rank judgment of the period: not being born in an excellent line is counted with illiteracy as making a life void

reading: A world that passes away in darkness, anger that speaks without knowing anything, and desire that sets love on things of no worth are named three that belong to a creature living in folly.
nuance: The three are the familiar triad of delusion, anger and desire, each given by what it does: delusion as a world gone dark, anger as speech without knowledge, desire as love for what is not wealth.

reading: One who seeks intimacy of desire with those who bear no friendship, the fool who neglects guarding his woman, and one who speaks words that slip from good character are named three who do not hold to right conduct.
nuance: பெண்பாலைக் காப்பிகழும் is read as a man neglecting to guard the woman of his house; the verse counts this as his own lapse of conduct.

norm.note: a gender norm of the period: a man's guarding of the woman of his house is treated as part of his conduct

reading: The disease of hunger that eats until wisdom fails, desire that arises so that self-restraint fails, and anger that cannot bear the hot words of enemies are named three as an army that drives out good deeds.
nuance: Hunger, a bodily need, stands in one army with two passions. Line 2 is read as செறிவு அழுங்க, restraint perishing, which the printed text's செறிவழங்க only half shows.

reading: The wife who knows her husband's mind, the ascetic who carries out what he has undertaken, and the king who shuns cruelty and does good are named three at whose word 'rain' the rain falls.
nuance: The wife's power is defined by her husband's intention, the ascetic's by his vows, the king's by his justice: each keeps the line of a station. Line 1 prints குறிப்பறிவான், a masculine form, for the wife.
domain_note: a wife, an ascetic and a king, one each

norm.note: a gender norm of the period: a wife's merit is defined by knowing and following her husband's mind

reading: Refusing the command of the five elders, false dealing within a whole and eager friendship, and abandoning the chaste wife settled in one's heart are named three as the acts of those without goodness.
nuance: நற்புடையிலாளர் is an unusual form, read as 'those who lack goodness'.

reading: The fire-priests living with dharma in mind, the fiercely angry king keeping to the path of just rule, and the wife going the way of her husband are named three as the seed of the month's three rains.
nuance: செந்தீ முதல்வர், those foremost at the red fire, names the fire-tending priests by their rite; the verse sets their dharma first and makes a priestly order, a royal order and a wife's obedience joint causes of the rains.
domain_note: priests, the king and a wife, one each

norm.note: norms of the period: the fire-priests' dharma and the wife's following of her husband are stated as causes of rain

reading: Living after forsaking the learned, the fool who acts on whatever he desires, and the babbler who does wrong unchecked are named three who will not reach the good world.
An army full of loyalty, a fortress that fears nothing however many gather against it, and great treasure laid up beyond counting are named three as the limbs of kings who rule the earth.
